translation: Tianzhuhuang (bamboo shavings, three liang), Xionghuang (realgar, two liang), Liujinu (Artemisia anomalae), Hongya (red sprout), Daji (Euphorbia, bone removed), Qilijie (dragon's blood, three liang each), Guiwei (Angelica tail, one liang five qian), Zhusha (cinnabar), Ercha (catechu, one liang each), Jing Ruxiang (pure frankincense, oil removed, three qian), Hupo (amber), Qingfen (calomel), Shuiyin (mercury, ground together with Qingfen until no stars are seen), Shexiang (musk, three qian each). Weigh out the above each in full measure, grind each into a fine powder; if true Tianzhuhuang is unavailable, substitute with three liang of true Danxing (Arisaema with bile). Then take twenty-four liang of good yellow wax, refine it until pure, set it in boiling water, throw in the medicine, stir evenly without stopping the hand, take it out and store it in a porcelain jar for later use. <ins>Zhenggu Zijin Dan</ins> (Bone-Setting Purple-Gold Pill, 正骨紫金丹) <ins>Wanling Gao</ins> (Myriad-Efficacy Plaster, 萬靈膏) (both seen in the injury of the vertex bone) <ins>Dingtong San</ins> (Pain-Relieving Powder, 定痛散) (seen in the injury of the shanjiao bone) <ins>Shuxue Wan</ins> (Blood-Dispersing Pill, 疏血丸) (seen in the injury of the lingyun bone).
